newsitem.title: UK: FOCUS-Royal says targets met as profits rise.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-Royal says targets met as profits rise.

text.p: Results at Royal & Sun Alliance Group marking the end of its first year of merged operations were overshadowed on Thursday by arguments about its success in tackling cases of pension misselling.

The British insurance giant, formed a year ago in a six billion pound ($9.6 billion) deal, was sticking to its guns that it had met a deadline set for it despite claims by financial regulator the Personal Investment Authority (PIA) that it had failed to do so.
Royal Sun deputy chairman Roger Taylor insisted that the company was committed to sorting out the problem and had met the timetable agreed with the PIA.
It had, he said, resolved 90 percent of priority one cases, which include people already retired or who have since died.
The PIA reiterated its belief that Royal Sun had failed to meet the deadline but said it would be talking to them in the future and declined to comment further.
The problems are believed to involve questions of what constitutes a completed case and what cases should be included to meet the PIA's first deadline.
Royal Sun said it had increased provisions to sort out cases of misselling in the late 1980s and early 1990s but declined to give figures. The company has nearly 15,000 cases to resolve.
Questions about the progress being made in the pension review came as the group reported an 11 percent rise in trading profits to 501 million pounds for the first six months of the year.
The dividend was raised 10 percent to 7.15 pence per share.
The strong pound, a major feature of the UK company reporting season so far, took some 25 million pounds off the headline figure.
Royal Sun confirmed it was still on target to deliver the 175 million pounds of annualised savings promised at the time of last year's merger.
Around 3,000 of the 5,000 targeted jobs have gone and annualised savings are running at some 95 million pounds.
The shares took heart from the above expectation figures, rising 20 1/2 pence to 543 pence by 1430 GMT.
Analysts predicted profit forecasts to rise with further support for the shares likely to come from the completion of a buyback already underway.
Chief executive Richard Gamble attributed the better than expected results to the U.S. and UK performances, particularly UK commercial property.
Tight underwriting and claims management bolstered the UK though the rating environment remains difficult and profits slipped slightly to 165 million pounds from 172 million pounds last year.
Personal motor insurance is the only area seeing a rise in rates and Royal Sun has put through increases of 10 percent in the last twelve months.
That has had a knock-on effect on exposures which are down seven percent year-on-year but the company said it was prepared to let non-profitable business go.

Like Commercial Union, which reported on Wednesday, costs from property subsidence were up. They increased by 19 million pounds to 56 million pounds, mainly as a result of the dry period between January and April.
General insurance profits worldwide rose 22 million pounds to 374 million pounds helped by an the performance in the U.S. and Canada.
The underwriting result improved by 51 million pounds to a loss of 81 million pounds.
U.S. profits rose 44 million pounds to 92 million pounds partly reflecting lower weather and catastrophe costs.
Now a top 10 operator in UK life business, Gamble said Royal Sun intended to be a major player but was cautious about acquisitions.
European life companies were 'extravagantly expensive', he said, and it was difficult to justify an acquisition benefiting shareholders.
Over the six months worldwide life profits, which now make up 21 percent of total operating profits, climbed 16 percent to 108 million pounds.

Royal Sun reaffirmed its commitment to active management of its capital base and the company has already began a repurchase of five percent of its shares. To date it has bought back some 32 million shares, less than half the amount planned.
The net asset value per share increased to 433 pence from 399 pence. As of August 4 it had risen further to 455 pence. ($ = 0.624 British Pounds)
